title: Go Maps: Key Facts for Interviews

scenes.line1: How do Go maps really work?
scenes.say: Maps are everywhere in Go code. But do you know the quirks that trip up candidates in interviews?

scenes.label: Reference
scenes.sub: Maps store key-value pairs and are reference types.
scenes.say: Maps in Go are reference types, which means changes affect all references to the same map.

rows.b: Can’t write, but reads return zero

scenes.say: If you read a key that’s not there, you get the zero value. Nil maps can’t be written to, but reads still return zero. Always check if a key exists with two-value assignment.

scenes.question: Are Go maps safe for concurrent writes?
scenes.right: No, regular maps are not safe. Use the sync.Map type for concurrent access.
scenes.say: Here’s a common trap: regular maps aren’t safe for concurrent writes. For that, Go gives you the sync.Map type.
